subject: Post-call exec recap: SolarTech discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@solartech.com>, Tony Ramirez <tony.ramirez@solartech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call exec recap: SolarTech discovery & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tony —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick executive recap from our discovery so you have a single place for the outcomes and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Search/assistant returning inconsistent product recommendations; long tail of edge cases causing manual support escalation (avg 18% of tickets).
- Business goal: Improve first-contact resolution and product upsell conversion; target ~30% reduction in manual ticketing and a 10% lift in conversion within 6 months.
- Technical constraints: Existing infra processes PII-filtering at ingestion, strict data retention policies, and preference for vendor-hosted with VPC options for regulated datasets.

Key risks called out by Tony
1) Security & compliance (SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest with customer KMS).
2) Predictable latencies for customer-facing features (need <200ms p95 for short prompts).
3) Procurement timeline & approvals (vendor onboarding and legal review).

Who we heard as decision-makers
- Executive sponsor: Tony Ramirez (CTO)
- Procurement & vendor mgmt: procurement@solartech.com
- Day-to-day champion: Sarah Nguyen (Product lead)

Next steps (action owners & timeline)
1) Marissa will share a concise SOW draft + security responses by EOD 5/22 (Marissa) — attached draft will include SLA options and dedicated capacity estimates.
2) SolarTech to share vendor onboarding form + initial SOC2 scope items (Sarah / procurement) — Sarah indicated vendor mgmt typically needs 10 business days.
3) Schedule a 30-min exec alignment (Tony + Laura + Marissa) week of 5/24 to confirm procurement path and SLA target. Proposed slots: Thu 5/27 10:00 or Fri 5/28 09:00 PT (Marissa).
4) Sean to prepare throughput/cost model for two scenarios (hosted vs. dedicated) ahead of the exec call.

Attachments referenced: SOW draft, security questionnaire template (placeholder). I attached the draft SOW and a copy of the security responses template to make procurement review easier.

If that looks right, I'll put the exec meeting on the calendar for Thu 5/27 10:00 PT and loop legal for the SOW review.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0187

Attachments: SolarTech_SOW_draft.pdf (draft), security_questionnaire_responses.xlsx (template)

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@solartech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tony Ramirez <tony.ramirez@solartech.com>, procurement@solartech.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call exec recap: SolarTech discovery & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed decision path: Tony (CTO) will give exec approval if legal/procurement sign off. Procurement typically runs a vendor packet and an initial security review (we've budgeted 15 business days for that).
- SOC2: we need the SOC2 Type II report (last 12 months) and a short summary of encryption/KMS processes.
- Latency: product is sensitive to p95; anything over 250ms is risky for our users. If you can provide a throughput/latency tradeoff table that would help.

I've attached our vendor onboarding form so you can see what procurement will ask. I'll start the packet with procurement but we'll need the SOW and security materials to move forward.

On meeting times: Tue 5/25 morning is tight for Tony. Thu 5/27 10:00 PT works today as proposed.

Sarah Nguyen
Sr. Product Manager, Customer Experience
SolarTech

Marissa — good write-up. A couple of internal asks before we lock the exec: 

- Escalation/Risk: Given the p95 latency sensitivity and SOC2 requirement, please include two purchase options in the SOW: (A) Hosted with reserved capacity + autoscaling and (B) Dedicated (permanent pool) with KMS integration. Call out expected unit costs and an estimated ramp plan.
- SLA: Procurement may ask for credits tied to p95. We should avoid open-ended credit exposure; propose a limited credit structure or tiered remediation tied to clear performance metrics.
- Legal: I'll have our contracts counsel pre-review the SOW draft. Please mark any nonstandard terms.

Sean — can you prepare the throughput/cost model for the two scenarios by EOD 5/24 so we can include in the deck?
